shared_elements: low-relief carving on the broad face of a standing stone
curved arm/limb elements rendered in shallow relief on the pillar's face
circular or ring-shaped motif on the body of the stone
belt-like or band-like horizontal element across the lower body
justification: Both show large upright pillars/slabs carved in shallow relief with anthropomorphic conventions: curved arms bending around the sides toward the front, a ring or disc motif at the centre of the torso, and a horizontal belt-like band lower down, which is a fairly specific shared scheme. The biggest difference is that B is an explicitly modelled head-and-body statue with facial features and dense surface decoration, whereas A's pillars are abstract T-shaped/plain blocks with only sparse isolated motifs (a small animal-like sign, a pitted panel) and include a separate carved ring-and-slab object on the ground with no counterpart in B.
